definitions.text: Vast plains in the central and southern part of the Argentine Republic in South America. The term is sometimes used in a wider sense for the plains extending from Bolivia to Southern Patagonia. Pampas cat (Zoöl.), a South American wild cat (Felis pajeros). It has oblique transverse bands of yellow or brown. It is about three and a half feet long. Called also straw cat. (Cervus, or Blastocerus, campestris). argenteum) with a silvery-white silky panicle. It is a native of the pampas of South America.
To feed to the full; to feed luxuriously; to glut; as, to pamper the body or the appetite. "A body . . . pampered for corruption." Dr. T. Dwight.
To gratify inordinately; to indulge to excess; as, to pamper pride; to pamper the imagination. South.
Fed luxuriously; indulged to the full; hence, luxuriant. "Pampered boughs." Milton. "Pampered insolence." Pope.
One who, or that which, pampers. Cowper.
A violent wind from the west or southwest, which sweeps over the pampas of South America and the adjacent seas, often doing great damage. Sir W. Parish.
A tribe of Indians inhabiting the pampas of South America.
A writing; a book. Testament of love. Sir Thomas More in his pamphlet of Richard the Third. Ascham.
A small book consisting of a few sheets of printed paper, stitched together, often with a paper cover, but not bound; a short essay or written discussion, usually on a subject of current interest.
To write a pamphlet or pamphlets. [R.] Howell.
A writer of pamphlets; a scribbler. Dryden. Macaulay.
To write or publish pamphlets. By pamphleteering we shall not win. C. Kingsley.
In the form of tendrils; -- applied especially to the spermatic and ovarian veins.
An ornament, composed of vine leaves and bunches of grapes, used for decorating spiral columns.
Having all the toes turned forward, as the colies.
